newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Puma H1 earnings undershoot forecasts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Puma H1 earnings undershoot forecasts.

text.p: German sportswear group Puma AG said on Friday that it expected sales growth below 10 percent this year after turnover increased six percent in the first half.

Analysts said that a 1.9 percent decline in second-quarter 1997 operating profits to 13.7 million marks ($7.5 million) undershot forecasts but first-half sales growth was in line with their expectations.

"First-half sales were in line with expectations. But the 1.9 percent decline in operating earnings in the second quarter was a little disappointing, we thought it might have been in line with sales growth," Ingbert Faust, analyst at UBS in Frankfurt, said.
Operating earnings grew 3.7 percent to 44.1 million marks in the first six months of 1997.
Analysts were waiting for a telephone conference call this afternoon before giving final judgement, particularly on how the company's marketing spend was shaping up.
"Overall we are expecting single-digit rate sales growth for the 1997 business year," Puma said in a statement.
Puma faces a difficult market environment in Europe at the moment, where the market is dominated by its neighbour and rival Adidas AG and the U.S. giant Nike.
Nike has taken an aggressive approach to the European market of late, targeting individual sports outlets.
"Adidas is too strong in Europe for this to have an effect, but it could affect Puma," Faust said.
Puma shares fell 1.36 percent to 50.60 marks in early electronic trade, while the overall index was rising. The share recovered somewhat during bourse trade to stand at 45 pfennigs at 51 marks.
One analyst said: "With the market as bullish as it is at the moment, if you come in slightly under expectations you will get slaughtered."

Faust said that one of the problems facing shares in Germany's MDAX index of medium-sized companies in the current bullish market was that if the share did not look like providing extremely high returns in a short time period, then people would stay in the blue-chips.
Puma said its sales reached 275.7 million marks in the first six months of the year and net profit advanced 6.1 percent to 41.2 million marks.
Orders in hand on June 30 were up 18.8 percent at 205.7 million marks, Puma said, with sports shoes accounting for a 13.2 percent rise, textiles for 32.4 percent and accessories for 58 percent.

But despite good orders, delays related to the start up of a new logistical centre in Germany slowed sales in May and June, the company said, and the effect would probably continue into the third quarter.
European sales in the first half, affected by the slowdown, were 185.1 million marks while Asia-Pacific sales rose 14.4 percent to 35.9 million marks.
American sales rose to 47.8 million marks from 34.6 million marks, mainly due to positive developments in Canada and a joint venture company in Chile. Sales in the U.S. were flat, Puma said.
